title: Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure
seo_title: Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure Class 11 Chemistry Worksheet (NCERT Ch 4)
standard_code: Class 11 Chemistry, Chapter 4: Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure
standard_text: Valence electrons, ionic bond, covalent bond, bond parameters, Lewis structure, polar character of covalent bond, covalent character of ionic bond, valence bond theory, resonance, geometry of covalent molecules, VSEPR theory, concept of hybridization involving s, p and d orbitals and shapes of some simple molecules, molecular orbital theory of homonuclear diatomic molecules (qualitative idea only), hydrogen bond.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 11 Chemistry worksheets for NCERT Chapter 4 Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure: octet rule, VSEPR shapes and bond angles, hybridisation, dipole moment, molecular orbital bond order and hydrogen bonding. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: VSEPR: electron pairs repel and get as far apart as possible.
body_html:
How to think about it

Atoms bond to reach stable configurations: by transferring electrons (ionic) or sharing them (covalent). VSEPR theory predicts shape from the electron pairs round the central atom; lone pairs repel more, so H₂O (104.5°) is bent and NH₃ (107°) pyramidal. Hybridisation sp, sp², sp³, sp³d and sp³d² gives linear, trigonal planar, tetrahedral, trigonal bipyramidal and octahedral arrangements.

Molecular orbital theory gives bond order ½(Nb − Na); O₂ has two unpaired electrons, so it is paramagnetic. Polar bonds can still give a non-polar molecule if the dipoles cancel (CO₂). Hydrogen bonds form between H and F, O or N.

Example

Bond order of N₂?

(10 − 4) ÷ 2

Answer: 3

Example

Hybridisation in BF₃?

3 bond pairs, no lone pair

Answer: sp²

Common mistakes

  • Giving CO₂ a dipole moment because its bonds are polar.
  • Forgetting lone pairs when naming shapes.
  • Saying O₂ is diamagnetic.

faq.a: Molecular orbital theory puts two unpaired electrons in its π* orbitals.

faq.q: Why is the bond angle of water less than 109.5°?
faq.a: Its two lone pairs repel the bonding pairs more strongly and push them together.

items.q: What is the hybridisation of carbon in C₆H₆ (each carbon)?
items.e: C₆H₆ (each carbon): sp².

items.q: Which is more covalent, AlCl₃ or NaCl?
items.e: Al³⁺ is small and highly charged.

items.q: What is the shape of BF<sub>3</sub>?

items.q: How many σ and π bonds are there in ethene, C₂H₄?

items.q: What is the order of repulsion in VSEPR theory?
c: lone pair–lone pair > lone pair–bond pair > bond pair–bond pair
bond pair–bond pair > lone pair–lone pair
lone pair–bond pair is the largest
items.e: So bond angles shrink when lone pairs are present.

items.q: What is the formal charge on each oxygen in the O₃ structure O=O⁺–O⁻? (the ends)

items.e: Formal charge = V − L − ½B.
